madeBy: backup/how-big-is-one-step-of-a-gain.py, backup/read-the-cut-side-again.py, backup/does-the-dent-move-with-the-width.py, backup/the-tone-control-nobody-prints.py, backup/build-gain-models.py, backup/run-gain-reproduce.py, backup/where-the-dent-lives.py, backup/write-gain-inference.py
claim: A gain byte printed -12 - +12 is decibels, one per step, offset by sixty-four. It answers over a window of twenty-five values from 52 to 76 and returns the nearest end for everything outside. And the two of them that forty-three types carry with no frequency printed beside either are this unit's equaliser's own shelf pair with the frequency byte taken away and pinned to its first printed entry.
whyNotNamed: There is nothing to name. The claim is a mapping from a byte to a number and a statement that two addresses on forty-three types are one filter measured elsewhere; neither is a structure with a name.
adds: The records say what each setting of a gain byte did to the level of each band. Nothing in them says the byte is decibels, that it is one per step, where the window is, that a departure at one setting belongs to the section rather than to the table, or that two addresses on forty-three types are a filter this archive has already measured somewhere else. Each of those is a comparison across records and the comparisons are made here: a boost half against the integers, a cut half against itself at two widths, and a tone control against an equaliser's shelves band for band.
refutedBy: A setting inside 52 to 76 whose gain is not the byte minus sixty-four decibels by more than a fifth of one, on a section that reads the gain rather than a flank, at more than one width. Or a type whose Low Gain profile at full boost is not the equaliser's low shelf at its first printed corner.
whatItWouldChange: A hundred and eighteen parameters across sixty-five types stop being unknown. Eighty-six of them are two shelves whose corners no page prints and which now have a measured profile at both of their gains' ends, taken from a type that does print its corners. A renderer that has the equaliser has the tone control.

eraPriors.claim: A filter gain is not one number the way an output level is, so a table of gains is a table of coefficient sets and costs what it costs multiplied by every frequency and every width the same section offers.
eraPriors.why: Twenty-five gains against sixteen centres and five widths is two thousand entries, and nothing of the period spends that on a tone control. But the coefficients are recomputed when a parameter changes and not per sample, so the control processor can afford here the arithmetic the audio path could not -- which is the opposite of what the same period implies about an output level, where the table is a hundred and twenty-eight bytes and a formula buys nothing.
eraPriors.wouldBeWrongIf: The measured decibels landed on a grid coarse enough to be a stored table rather than on the integers. They land on the integers on the boost half to a tenth of a decibel, and the one setting that does not lands back on them at another width.

eraPriors.claim: A control marked in decibels steps in decibels, and twenty-five settings out of a hundred and twenty-eight means something maps a printed range onto a stretch of the byte and refuses the rest.
eraPriors.why: Where that stretch sits is measurable rather than arguable, and this unit's other classes have already turned out to work that way: a width byte with five entries that returns the first for anything past them, a rate byte whose last two settings have no entry of their own.
eraPriors.wouldBeWrongIf: The byte went on answering outside 52 to 76. Three settings past each end return the same figure as the end itself.

alternatives.reading: The two shelves are the pair these two types carry and not the pair the class carries. Forty-three types print this address and two are read.
alternatives.ruledOutBy: The run it asked for, on a delay whose feedback is parked at nothing and whose damping is at bypass, so its effect path returns one copy of the note and colours nothing. Both shelves hinge where the other two hinge -- five kilohertz, on all four readings -- and the profiles lie on each other to a mean of three hundredths of a decibel on the low gain and eight on the high, over twenty-two bands. One band disagrees: the topmost, on the high gain's cut, by 0.72 of a decibel. It is the reading's floor and not the type. The same shelf pushed the other way at the same band agrees to 0.06, and a shelf that belonged to the type would differ both ways -- a cut takes the top band down towards the silence and a boost takes it up away from it, and this run's takes stand nine decibels closer to the silence than the run it is being held against. Every band with room on both agrees to 0.12 or better.

alternatives.reading: The multiplier steps evenly across the byte and the decibels are whatever that lands on, which is what a section built as a scaled band-pass summed with the dry gives.
alternatives.ruledOutBy: Read as the height of the feature it is out by a mean 0.046 of the span against 0.010 for the step law, and its worst record is 0.170 against 0.032. Read over the whole profile it comes first on the median and leans on 3 records where the step law leans on 0. Coming first while leaning is being beaten, and it is beaten under the reading the class's own quantity lives in.

alternatives.reading: The byte is decibels offset by sixty-four over all hundred and twenty-eight settings and the printed range is where the panel stops.
alternatives.ruledOutBy: Three settings past each end of the window return the same figure as the end itself, to within a twentieth of a decibel, on a section that reads the gain rather than a flank of it. The byte does not reach sixty-four decibels of cut; it stops at twelve and stays there.

alternatives.reading: The twenty-five settings are a stored table of near-decibels rather than the integers, and the departures on the cut half are its entries.
alternatives.ruledOutBy: The largest departure is at one setting and it is gone at another width, where the same setting lands on the law. An entry of a table cannot depend on the width byte. What is left after that is a boost half on the law to 0.15 dB and a cut half whose remaining departures are two tenths, which is what one of these readings resolves at the peak and is not a table.

separatedBy.observable: Whether a departure repeats at the same byte across widths, centres and sections.
separatedBy.what_the_run_returned: Four mirrored pairs at two widths. The one that departs at the first width lands on the law at the second and nothing else moves by half as much.
separatedBy.why_not_separable: Only for the departures under two tenths of a decibel, which are the size of what this reading resolves at the peak band. Telling a table of near-decibels from the integers there needs a reading finer than a twelfth-octave band profile of a held note, and the archive has already measured that reading finer scatters rather than sharpens on this type.

alternatives.reading: A peaking section's cut is its boost inverted, so mirrored settings have the same height.
alternatives.ruledOutBy: It holds on the shelves and not on the peaking sections. The tone control's cut is its boost negated to a median 0.02 dB over twenty-two bands. The peaking section's mirrored pair at nine decibels is 0.46 dB apart at one width and 0.14 at another, where its other three pairs are within a quarter of a decibel at both. One structure inverted cannot be apart at all, and cannot be apart by an amount that changes with the width.

reproduces.what_survived_twice: One candidate and no verdict. `decibels-are-the-byte-minus-sixty-four` is the ranking's winner read as a height and the only candidate that does not lean read as a profile; the multiplier candidate is beaten under the first and leans under the second. Neither reading returns `reproduces` for anything, so the class stands on the mapping and does not close on the model. What stops it is stated and is not the byte: the model renders a peaking cut as the exact mirror of its boost and this unit does not, which is a topology this class is not about and the equaliser class now carries as an open reading.

charts.why: Two states and the boundary is between 0 and 1: one value of the byte selects one corner and the other 127 select the other. The figure is the half point of the deviation, which is where this model's corner parameter is defined.
